about: Operating scenarios with good practice explained, written for this app.

scenarios.situation: You've found a quiet spot and want to call CQ.
choices: Call CQ straight away
Send QRL? first and listen
Send your callsign a few times to test
scenarios.why: A frequency can sound empty when one side of a contact is too weak for you to hear. Send QRL? (is this frequency in use?), listen, and try once more before calling CQ.

scenarios.situation: A rare station sends 'TU UP 2' and you can't hear any callers.
choices: Call on their frequency
Transmit 2 kHz higher and keep listening on theirs
Ask them to QSY
scenarios.why: UP 2 means they're listening about 2 kHz above their own frequency. Call there, and keep your receiver on them. Calling on their frequency drowns them out for everyone.

scenarios.situation: The DX station sends 'K1?' and your call is G4ABC.
choices: Call anyway: they might hear you
Stay quiet until they finish with K1
Send 'G4ABC G4ABC G4ABC'
scenarios.why: They've picked out part of a call starting K1 and are asking only for it. Calling over them slows everything down and is the quickest way to annoy a pileup.

scenarios.situation: Someone answers your CQ much faster than you can copy.
choices: Give up and say nothing
Send QRS (please send more slowly)
Pretend you copied and send 73
scenarios.why: QRS is a normal, polite request, and most operators are happy to slow down. It's better than a contact where neither side got anything.

scenarios.situation: You want to answer a station calling CQ.
choices: Answer wherever your dial happens to be
Zero-beat them first so you reply on their frequency
Answer 1 kHz off to be heard clearly
scenarios.why: Many operators use narrow filters. If you reply off-frequency they may not hear you at all. Match their note to your sidetone first.

scenarios.situation: You've finished a contact and want to sign off properly.
choices: Just stop sending
Send your call and SK
Send 73 three times
scenarios.why: Identify with your callsign (most licences require it at the end of each contact) and send SK to show the contact is over.

scenarios.situation: You need to tune your antenna tuner on the air.
choices: Tune on the DX station's frequency so you're ready
Find a clear frequency, check it's free, use low power and keep it short
Tune at full power while calling CQ
scenarios.why: Tuning on top of others causes interference. Pick a clear spot, check it's free, keep the power low and the carrier brief.

scenarios.situation: A DX station has a huge pileup and you're not getting through.
choices: Call continuously
Listen to their pattern (where they're listening, how fast) and call at the right moment
Increase speed so you stand out
scenarios.why: Good DXers listen more than they send. Learn where the DX is listening and when they come back, then call once or twice at the right moment.
